newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. stocks seen in near-term pullback.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. stocks seen in near-term pullback.

text.p: Thursday's powerful reversal on Wall Street is an indication U.S. stocks are likely in the midst of a near-term correction, technical analysts said on Friday.
Some technicians see the coming weeks bringing a "consolidation" phase in stocks, without a major downdraft. Others see a pullback of five or even 10 percent in the works.
A sharp New Year's rally pushed the Dow industrials up over seven percent in January through Thursday's intraday high but also set up stocks for a round of profit taking, they said.

"We have been pushing into overbought territory, especially this week," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities. "We're probably going into some kind of trading range environment for the near term."

The Dow hit an intra-day high of 6907 on Thursday, pushing through the 6900 psychological barrier for the first time. But stocks quickly reversed and tumbled 164 points from its high to its session low, before closing down 94 at 6756.
The Dow was off about 50 at 6706 in early afternoon trading on Friday.
The move was given added technical significance by Thursday's record New York Stock Exchange volume of 684 million shares, analysts said.
"I think it's a short-term turning point," said Peter Green, vice president of technical research at Gruntal & Co.
He noted that Thursday's Dow move "engulfed" the highs and lows of the previous four sessions, a bearish sign.
Green said that in the near-term the stock market may follow the bond market's path.
"The bond market is about five percent off its high and if the stock market declines about five percent off its high, it would not be out of the realm of the possible," he said.
Following the pullback, stocks would likely make a new run back to their highs set this week, or slightly below them, Green said.
A pause now is likely in the rally that has catapulted the Dow up 28 percent from its July lows, Richard McCabe, chief technical analyst at Merrill Lynch, told Reuters Financial Television.
"The weakness in the past day or day-and-a-half I think may be kind of lead-in or a prelude for a late-winter pullback, which might be around 10 percent, give or take a little bit," McCabe said.

But the power of the recent advance, as measured in volume and the advance/decline line, indicates the 10 percent dip would likely give way to a renewed advance, McCabe said. This could lead to a "moderate" new high in the spring, he said.
But the new high in spring will give way to a potentially bigger decline in stocks, said McCabe, whose firm has forecast a correction of up to 25 percent in 1997.

More bullish analysts, while acknowledging the market is under near-term pressure, said over the longer term the market will be supported by the strong U.S. economy, corporate earnings and low interest rates.
But a sharp upturn in interest rates could change the bullish scenario.
"Stocks have handled gradually rising rates," said Nie at EVEREN Securities said. "Rapidly rising rates is a different hurdle."
